text: After lecture Professor R stopped me and said that sweater really suits my figure, and that I should wear it to office hours more often. I laughed it off and left.

moments.quote: that sweater really suits my figure
moments.why: These words comment on your figure and clothing.

review.summary: You described a comment about your figure and wearing that sweater to office hours. You laughed it off and left, and it is understandable to notice how that felt.

text: Professor R emailed me at 9:40 at night: Your midterm was disappointing, but I think we can find a way to fix that. Come by my office after hours on Friday when it is quiet. Do not mention this to the TA.

moments.quote: Your midterm was disappointing, but I think we can find a way to fix that.
moments.why: These words link your midterm result to an unspecified way to fix it.

moments.quote: Come by my office after hours on Friday when it is quiet.
moments.why: These words invite you to meet after hours when it is quiet.

moments.quote: Do not mention this to the TA.
moments.why: These words ask you to keep the meeting from another person.

review.summary: You received a late-night message about your midterm that asked you to meet after hours and not tell the TA. It is understandable to notice the secrecy and timing in those words.

text:
[owner] Watch me.
[other] So about your essay.
[owner] I wanted to ask how I could get it up to an A.
[other] It's close.
[other] We could talk about it over drinks at my place this weekend.
[owner] I'd rather go over it here if that's okay.
[other] Suit yourself.
[other] But B students don't usually get recommendation letters.

moments.quote: We could talk about it over drinks at my place this weekend.
moments.why: The words invite you to discuss schoolwork alone at a home, off site and over drinks.

moments.quote: But B students don't usually get recommendation letters.
moments.why: The words link a recommendation letter opportunity to your current grade after you declined the meeting.

moments.quote: But B students don't usually get recommendation letters.
moments.why: The words suggest a worse outcome immediately after you said you would rather meet at school.

review.summary: You asked how to improve your essay and were invited to talk about it over drinks at their place, which you declined. After you declined, a comment was made about B students not usually getting recommendation letters.

text: In the Monday meeting my manager said, look how dressed up she is today, someone's trying to get promoted. Everyone laughed. I didn't say anything.

moments.quote: look how dressed up she is today, someone's trying to get promoted
moments.why: The words comment on your clothing and appearance in front of others.

moments.quote: look how dressed up she is today, someone's trying to get promoted
moments.why: The words link a woman's clothing to trying to get promoted.

review.summary: You described a meeting comment about how you were dressed, followed by laughter from others. That kind of remark can match descriptions of comments about appearance and sex.
